FEIE PHYSICAL PRESENCE CALCULATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Have you been abroad 330 days yet?

List your stays in foreign countries. You get your best 12-month window, how many of the 330 full days you have, how many days you can still spend elsewhere, the first date you reach 330, and the prorated foreign earned income exclusion for the tax year.

Your dates, not tax advice. Every value is editable and nothing is uploaded: dates are used in this browser tab only.

Your stays abroad

One stay per line, first and last full day inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD. Leave out the days you travelled: a day counts only if you were in a foreign country from midnight to midnight.

The 12-month window may start before your first foreign day. Count only full 24-hour days, keep passport stamps, flight records and a calendar, and check the result with Form 2555 instructions or a tax professional before filing.

Common questions

How many days do I need for the physical presence test?

330 full days in a foreign country within any 12 consecutive months. A full day is 24 hours from midnight to midnight, so a day you fly in or out does not count. On the sample dates the best 12-month span holds 347 full foreign days, 17 more than needed, so up to 35 days of that span could be spent anywhere else.

Can the 12 months start on any day?

Yes: the 12-month period does not have to be a calendar year and can start on any day, so the calculator slides a 12-month window across your dates and reports the one with the most foreign days. It also reports the first date a window holds 330 days (2025-09-04 on the sample).

How much income can I exclude?

Up to the annual limit ($130,000 for 2025, entered as an editable figure), prorated by the days of the tax year that fall in your qualifying period and never more than your foreign earned income. On the sample, $95,000 of income is fully excluded. Check the current limit and your eligibility with the IRS or a tax professional.

Is this tax advice?

No. It counts the days you type and nothing is uploaded. It does not decide whether you have a tax home abroad, what counts as earned income, or whether to elect the exclusion, and it is not a substitute for Form 2555 instructions or a qualified professional.

FEIE Physical Presence Calculator · guide

The 330-day physical presence test: how to count it

Short answer: you need 330 full days in a foreign country inside some 12-month period, and the period can start on any day. That leaves at most 35 days of the 365 for travel and the United States.

Everything below is arithmetic on invented dates. Not tax, legal or immigration advice. The foreign earned income exclusion has further requirements, including a tax home in a foreign country and foreign earned income. Check the current IRS figures.

A worked example

Four stays in Lisbon: 2024-09-15 to 2025-01-20, 2025-02-03 to 2025-05-30, 2025-06-12 to 2025-09-28 and 2025-10-05 to present (as of 2026-02-28), with $95,000 of foreign earned income for 2025.

  • The best 12-month window runs 2025-02-03 to 2026-02-02 and holds 347 full foreign days: 17 more than the 330 needed, so 35 days of that window could be spent elsewhere.
  • The first date any 12-month span holds 330 foreign days is 2025-09-04.
  • For 2025 the exclusion limit entered is $130,000. All 365 days of 2025 fall in a qualifying span, so the prorated limit is $130,000.00 and the whole $95,000.00 is excluded.

How to keep your count honest

  • Use full days only: remove the days you flew in or out of each stay.
  • Keep passport stamps, boarding passes and a calendar for every trip.
  • A short US trip eats into your 35 spare days; list each stay separately and see which window still holds 330.
  • Prorating: if your qualifying period covers only part of the tax year, the limit is cut by the share of the year it covers.

Common questions

How do I count a full day abroad?

A full day is a 24-hour period from midnight to midnight spent in a foreign country. The day you fly out and the day you land are not full days, and neither are days over international waters or in the United States.

Does the 12-month period have to be a calendar year?

No. It can start on any day. Try every start date and use the one with the most full foreign days, which is what the calculator does.

Is this tax advice?

No. It is arithmetic on invented dates. Check Form 2555 instructions or a qualified professional. No warranty.

No warranty. Provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind. Not tax, legal or immigration advice. Not affiliated with the IRS or any tax preparer or expat service. Best-effort hosting, no SLA.
